title: Insurers told to lift their game
full_text:
Australia’s insurers are facing a revved-up corporate regulator, which says many are treating their car insurance customers with contempt.
The Australian Securities & Investments Commission said the most complained-about insurance product in Australia was comprehensive motor vehicle cover.
The regulator’s review of the sector found that none of the eight car insurers it surveyed explained to their customers the key factors that affected how they calculated premiums or why they’d changed from the year prior. Premiums for car insurance grew 42 per cent between 2019 and 2024, and have continued to soar.
ASIC said it had serious concerns about the way insurers were dealing with their car cover customers in a warning to the industry, which could point to potential court action. Already ASIC has secured several wins against the major insurers over their handling and pricing of discounts to customers.
But ASIC commissioner Alan Kirkland said the regulator’s latest probe into the pricing of car insurance showed the big insurers were clearly unclear in the information they provided to customers. This included insurers not telling customers if they paid their insurance annually, rather than monthly, they could secure a cheaper premium, by as much as 20 per cent.
ASIC said insurers should start clearly disclosing premium costs in any renewal notices.
In addition, ASIC found many Australians with car insurance didn’t know they could secure a discount on their premiums if they switched to a different provider. This was resulting in many customers paying more for their insurance than they otherwise could, with many unknowingly being squeezed over their car cover.
ASIC found insurers offered generic explanations or none at all. “This fails to meet the needs of customers trying to understand the reasons for significant price increases,’ Mr Kirkland said.
He told The Australian ASIC’s findings were a “clear warning” to the insurance sector.
He said they had to “lift their game”.
“I think insurers should see that as a sign they need to do a lot better.” The ASIC commissioner pointed to the regulator’s track record in taking legal action against Australia’s insurers.
“We will continue to do that if we find misleading prices or practices,” Mr Kirkland said.
But he declined to say if the insurers were delivering misleading prices. Price is a key reason Australians change their car insurance, but often insurers make it difficult to understand.
Australia’s listed insurers Suncorp, QBE, and Insurance Australia Group are due to report their earnings over the coming week.
Macquarie analysts noted IAG was expected to deliver a $1.03bn full-year profit, while rival Suncorp is also expected to report $1bn in profits. Mr Kirkland refused to take a view on whether Australia’s insurers were too profitable, noting ASIC hadn’t “looked into the financials”.
